correctness.rationale: The function ax+bxy+cx²y+dy has a unique pole of order seven on supersingular elliptic E:y²+y=x³ because x,y have pole orders two and three and c!=0; Artin–Schreier degree-two cover is smooth and Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus five. For q=4^m, N_m=1+2# elliptic (x,y) with Tr(ax+bxy+cx²y+dy)=0; this is a complete finite calculation for m=1..5. Independent Python code independently reconstructed field models and enumerated all 192 tuples for all 5 extensions, obtaining precisely the fourteen given (multiplicity,c1..c5) rows. Newton identities recover first five Weil coefficients and the genus-five q-functional equation supplies the other five; all 14 2-adic Newton hulls match the two given profiles, and finite-field Tate isogeny theorem equates equal polynomials with F4-isogeny. No finite-field search extrapolated beyond F4-valued coefficients.

originality.rationale: Dragutinović 2025 preprint (and 2026 published version) introduces exactly the genus-five family and explicitly identifies supersingular c=b² locus (under its alternative coefficient naming); this part is prior. Its inspected Theorem/Corollary 4.4 cover geometric supersingularity/generic Newton polygons and an F2 example, not a complete frequency table of fourteen Frobenius polynomials for all F4 tuples. An earlier paper enumerates genus-five curves over F2, not this F4 quadruple census. General LMFDB isogeny classes catalogue may contain individual polynomials, but listing classes alone does not give parameter-to-class multiplicities; no exact table in inspected indexed sources.

value.rationale: A finite yet naturally complete arithmetic census for the first quadratic coefficient extension quantifies all fourteen represented F4 isogeny classes and their frequencies, and shows a sharp two-stratum Newton polygon dichotomy within this specified 192-tuple family. These concrete isogeny frequencies and restricted absence of 1/4 slopes are useful refinements of the motivating geometric classification, not an arbitrary low-value spot check.

final_claim: For all 192 tuples (a,b,c,d) in F4^4 with c!=0, the smooth genus-five curves y²+y=x³, u²+u=ax+bxy+cx²y+dy realize exactly fourteen distinct F4 Hasse–Weil numerator polynomials with the given exhaustive multiplicity table and hence fourteen F4 Jacobian isogeny classes. Exactly 48 have supersingular Newton polygon (1/2)^10 with c=b²; remaining 144 have slopes (1/3)^3,(1/2)^4,(2/3)^3.
limitations: All 192 F4 coefficient tuples with c≠0, not modded out by isomorphism; no NP statement for algebraic-closure parameters or F4^m coefficients.
No classification of isomorphism classes, principal polarizations, or actual isogeny maps; exhaustive point counts limited to five required extensions and enough by Weil functional equation.
